question: The loss of water in the form of water droplets from leaves of plants is called _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Guttation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guttation** is the process by which water is expelled from the edges of leaves of certain plants in the form of droplets.
 
• This occurs primarily during the night when soil moisture levels are high, and transpiration is low.
 
• It is different from **transpiration**, which is the evaporation of water from plant surfaces, mainly through stomata.
 
• Guttation usually occurs through specialized structures called **hydathodes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pressure gradient** refers to the difference in hydrostatic pressure that drives the movement of water and nutrients within plant tissues.
 
• **Plasmolysis** is the process where cells lose water in a hypertonic solution, causing the cell membrane to pull away from the cell wall.
 
• **Translocation** is the movement of nutrients and other solutes within the plant, typically through the phloem.
 
• The process of guttation is most commonly observed in **grasses, strawberries, and some herbaceous plants**.
